name: Governance and corpus legal simulator
note: Built against the placeholder, in parallel with the venue rather than as a subtree of it. Corpus scanned 2026-08-29: generic federal statute text and public case law (Title VI, § 1983, 17 U.S.C. § 201, FERPA, a template enabling act), no personal names, no student records, no institution-specific provisions. The collision is architectural, not content.

survival.duration: indefinite — statute text and case law age slowly
survival.survives_gallery: yes — the corpus is a document set, not an installation
survival.irl_contingency: Runs from a static file server, NOT from file:// — corrected 2026-08-29 by the engineering vantage against this file's earlier claim that it runs offline. 14 requests, all same-origin: no font, no CDN, no analytics, no API, no dependencies installed. The real no-browser contingency is sim/cli.mjs, which is text.
survival.note: Earlier entry here overstated survivability. Corrected against measurement supplied by the project itself.

partial_compliance: Fully resolved. Merged the shell at af83ccd, dropped the contested edits, re-added its card in the shell's idiom on its own branch, adopted the officer-corpus model at ba2422b, and retargeted PR #3 to the venue branch. P7, P8 and P13 all clear against it.
merged_upstream: af83ccd — merged the venue shell; adopted the officer-corpus model at ba2422b
_owner_note: This file is owned by the project it describes. The venue assembles it and never edits another project's copy; a sibling edits only its own. That is the whole point of the split.
